Nonmetric multidimensional scaling

Source: R/svt.R
nmdsf.Rd

Kruskal's nonmetric scaling: at each step the distances of the current configuration are fitted by a monotone (isotonic, pool-adjacent- violators) regression on the order of the dissimilarities, and one SMACOF step (smacf()) is taken towards the fitted disparities, until no coordinate moves by tol. The stress is Kruskal's stress-1 of the last step. The start is normal from seed 42, as set.seed() takes it.

Usage

nmdsf(D, ndim = 2, maxit = 300, tol = 1e-06)

Arguments

D

A symmetric matrix of dissimilarities.

ndim

The number of dimensions.

maxit

The most steps.

tol

The convergence tolerance on the largest change of a coordinate.

Value

A list of class nmdsf: coords, stress, iter and conv.

References

Kruskal, J. B. (1964). Nonmetric multidimensional scaling: a numerical method. Psychometrika, 29(2), 115-129. doi:10.1007/BF02289694

See also

Other scaling: amscal(), anchv(), anomin(), bamscl(), bbscal(), bmdsf(), bunfld(), cjrirt(), cmdsf(), cutlns(), dblctr(), dwnom(), dynirt(), indscl(), ipsrec(), irtem(), irtlik(), irtpst(), mdsfit(), mlsmu(), nombt(), nomll(), nompr(), nomutl(), nrmvec(), optcls(), ordirt(), ordocl(), procrs(), scboot(), smacf(), smunf(), unfstr(), votagr(), wrdfsh()

Examples

set.seed(1)
D <- as.matrix(dist(matrix(rnorm(40), 10)))
nmdsf(D, maxit = 50)$stress
#> [1] 0.1259758
